title: Add Live Shared Departures to Your Website with a Tour Booking Widget
excerpt: Add a tour booking widget to your website with one snippet: live shared departures, every booking credited to your agency. No fee to join; Sawa takes 10%.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

You add live tour departures to your website with Sawa's booking widget: one iframe snippet that shows forming and confirmed shared departures on your own pages. Paste it into WordPress, Wix, Squarespace or a hand-coded site and it picks up your page's colours. Every booking is credited to your agency's referral code, and approved agencies get the snippet in the Promote section of their dashboard. There is no fee to join or list, and Sawa takes 10% of the selling price.

The Egyptian Travel Agents Association provides an independent place to check agency membership.

Key facts

Fact Detail
What it is An embeddable widget that shows Sawa's forming and confirmed shared departures on your own website
Install One iframe snippet pasted into WordPress, Wix, Squarespace or hand-coded HTML. No developer and no build step
Widget addresses /embed?ref=YOUR-CODE (full catalogue banner) · /embed/tour/TOUR-ID (one day tour) · /embed/package/PACKAGE-ID (one package)
Styling Automatic colours from your page; for anything more, ask us on WhatsApp
Attribution Every traveller who books through your widget is credited to your agency's referral code
Cost No fee to join or list, and no widget fee. Sawa takes 10% of the selling price. Selling agencies earn a share of the pool for the seats they sell, paid as set in the agency agreement
Prices Fixed per traveller, however the group fills
Requirements A Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration, passenger and liability insurance, a track record and a payout account
Group size A date confirms at four travellers; eight at most
Review Usually two to four business days, then an onboarding call

Your agency's website already gets visitors who want group tours, but a departure only runs once it fills. One snippet of HTML puts the live shared departures on Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure marketplace, onto your own pages, and every booking made through it is credited to your agency's referral code. This post is written for Egyptian tour operators. It explains what the widget shows your visitors, gives the embed code, walks through the three-step setup, and covers styling, referral credit and what you need to qualify.

How can I add live tour departures to my website?

Use an embeddable departures widget. Sawa's is a single iframe tag you paste into any page. It lists live, bookable shared departures and works on WordPress, Wix, Squarespace and hand-coded sites. Your visitors browse forming and confirmed departures and can join from your page. Sawa handles the matching and the confirmation, and payments go through Online Era as agent.

One thing to be clear about from the start: the widget shows departures from Sawa's fixed catalogue, on Sawa's calendar and at Sawa's prices. It is not a way to publish tours of your own.

What the Sawa widget shows your visitors

The widget shows real shared departures: dates still forming, and dates already confirmed with a GoAhead, the moment four travellers have reserved a date and it is set to run. Prices are per person and fixed per traveller, however the group fills. Reserving is free and needs no card, and nothing is charged before the GoAhead.

The embed code

The widget installs with a single iframe tag. The catalogue-banner version reads:

<iframe src="https://sawa.tours/embed?ref=YOUR-CODE" style="width:100%;border:0;border-radius:18px" loading="lazy" data-sawa-embed></iframe>

loading="lazy" tells browsers to fetch the widget only when a visitor scrolls it into view. Your dashboard's Promote section gives you the snippet with your referral code already filled in, so copy the final version from there instead of editing the example above.

Widget address What it shows your visitors
/embed?ref=YOUR-CODE A Sawa banner leading to the whole shared-departures catalogue
/embed/tour/TOUR-ID?ref=YOUR-CODE One day tour, with its fixed per-traveller price
/embed/package/PACKAGE-ID?ref=YOUR-CODE One multi-day package, with its fixed per-traveller price

Setup in three steps

Setup takes three steps, none of them technical.

  1. Open Promote. Once your agency is approved, the Promote section of your dashboard shows your referral code and ready-made snippets with the code filled in.
  2. Paste the snippet. Copy the iframe into your page's HTML, or into your site builder's HTML or embed block. The widget page shows the snippet and the three addresses.
  3. Publish. Open the published page on desktop and on a phone and check the widget displays as you want before you promote it.

Styling: how the widget matches your brand

The widget takes its colours from your page automatically, so there is no theme to maintain. The frame arrives borderless and full-width, with rounded 18-pixel corners. For customisation beyond the automatic colours, ask us on WhatsApp.

  • Give it a real page. A dedicated "Group tours" page gives the widget room and gives travellers one address to share and revisit.
  • Keep body colours clean. The widget follows your page's colours, so a high-contrast, readable palette carries over best.
  • Check the phone view. Open the published page on a phone before you promote it.

Referral credit: how bookings come back to your agency

Every traveller who books through your widget is credited to your agency's referral code, so the traffic you already have is counted as yours.

The widget is a referral channel, not a handover. A visitor your marketing already paid for can join a shared departure from your own page, and the booking is credited to your code as a seat you sold. As a selling agency you earn a share of the pool for the seats you sell. Calculations are in Egyptian pounds and agencies are paid in euros, on the timing set in the agency agreement.

Sawa runs the operation afterwards. The date confirms at four travellers. On a day tour, a 10% deposit is due by payment link at the GoAhead and the balance 2 days before departure; a forming date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four, and if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and another date is suggested. On a package, the deposit is 25%, the balance is due 14 days before, and four travellers are needed by 30 days before. The traveller's contract is with the operating agency, one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due; Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241) collects the payment as agent for it, in euros.

What the widget costs and what you need to qualify

There is no fee to join or list on Sawa, and no fee for installing or running the widget. Sawa takes 10% of the selling price. You need an approved agency account, which requires a Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration and passenger and liability insurance. The application also asks for a track record (two references, or a portfolio of past tours with review links) and a payout account. Newer agencies are welcome but must show references or a portfolio. We check the documents and confirm the licence with the Ministry.

After you apply through Sawa's operator page and the verification form, review usually takes two to four business days. An onboarding call follows, after which you go live and can pick up your widget snippet.

How to get the widget with Sawa Tours

Sawa Tours is a marketplace, not a tour operator, operated by Online Era (registration 148500). It pools travellers from several licensed Egyptian agencies onto the same date of a fixed tour, and the date is confirmed when four travellers have reserved it. The operating agency, one of the licensed agencies with travellers on the date, runs the tour under its own licence, and it also earns the pool share on seats it sold itself. Sawa runs the matching and the confirmation, and the widget puts those live dates on your website. For the wider model, read shared departures for Egyptian tour operators.

To get it, apply through Sawa's operator page with your licence, ETAA registration and insurance. Once approved, your dashboard's Promote section and the widget page hold your snippets. Travellers can browse open departures and how the model works, and the team answers on WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613.

The verdict for operators

One pasted snippet puts Sawa's live departures on your site, follows your page's colours and credits every booking to your referral code, with no developer and no fee to join. Next step: apply through Sawa's operator page, then copy your snippet from the Promote section of your dashboard. The widget page has the snippet. Questions first? Message the team on WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613.

faq.q: Does the Sawa widget cost anything to install or use?
faq.a: No. There is no fee to join or list on Sawa and no widget fee. Sawa takes 10% of the selling price, and selling agencies earn a share of the pool for the seats they sell, paid as set in the agency agreement. The snippets come with an approved agency account.

faq.q: Can I show just one tour instead of the whole catalogue?
faq.a: Yes. The widget comes in three addresses: /embed?ref=YOUR-CODE for a banner leading to the whole catalogue, /embed/tour/TOUR-ID for a single day tour, and /embed/package/PACKAGE-ID for one multi-day package. Each takes your referral code, so every booking stays credited to your agency either way.

faq.q: Do I need a developer to add the widget to my website?
faq.a: No. The widget is one iframe snippet that you paste into your page's HTML or your site builder's embed block. There is no build step and nothing to host. The Promote section of your dashboard gives you the snippet with your referral code already filled in.

faq.q: Will the widget slow down my website?
faq.a: It should not be noticeable. The iframe carries loading="lazy" , so browsers fetch it only when a visitor scrolls it into view, and the widget's code runs inside the frame rather than in your page. As with any embed, test the finished page on a slow connection.

faq.q: What happens after a traveller books through my widget?
faq.a: The booking is credited to your agency's referral code, and the traveller joins a shared departure on Sawa. Nothing is charged until that date reaches four travellers, the GoAhead. On a day tour a 10% deposit is then due, and the balance 2 days before departure; on a package the deposit is 25% and the balance is due 14 days before. If a day-tour date has not reached four by 7 days before the tour, it is cancelled and nothing is charged. The tour itself is run by the operating agency, named before the deposit is due.

faq.q: What do I need before applying for an agency account?
faq.a: A Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration and passenger and liability insurance. The application also asks for two references or a portfolio of past tours with review links, and a payout account. Newer agencies are welcome but must show references or a portfolio.

faq.q: Can I match the widget to my site's design?
faq.a: The colours are automatic: the widget takes them from your page, so there is no styling configuration to keep up to date. The frame arrives with a rounded 18-pixel border radius. For anything beyond the automatic colours, ask us on WhatsApp.
